**Observation Log:**

[TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/02/02 (Thu) 04:45  
[USER] User inquired about whether certain types of sunscreen can clog pores and cause breakouts.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Certain types of sunscreen can clog pores and cause breakouts due to comedogenic ingredients.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Comedogenic ingredients include heavy oils, fragrances, and certain types of silicones that can trap sweat and bacteria in the skin.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] It is essential to choose a sunscreen labeled "non-comedogenic" or "oil-free" and with a lightweight formula.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Thoroughly cleansing the skin after wearing sunscreen is important to remove any residue that may cause breakouts.  
[USER] User noted that even non-comedogenic sunscreens can still cause breakouts and asked about specific ingredients to look for or avoid.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended looking for sunscreens labeled "oil-free," "non-comedogenic," and "fragrance-free" to prevent breakouts.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested avoiding sunscreens with heavy oils, lanolin, or mineral oil as these are comedogenic.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Advised avoiding sunscreens with high levels of silicones, which can trap sweat and bacteria in the skin.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended considering mineral-based sunscreens containing zinc and titanium dioxide, which are less likely to cause breakouts.  
[USER] User expressed surprise at the number of ingredients to consider in sunscreen and asked about the effect of SPF level on breakouts.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Clarified that the SPF level does not directly affect the likelihood of getting breakouts.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Explained that SPF indicates UVB protection against sunburns but does not relate to clogged pores.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Mentioned that some higher SPF sunscreens may contain more pore-clogging ingredients, while lower SPF sunscreens may have more fragrances or irritants.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Emphasized the importance of finding a sunscreen that suits the user's skin type to maintain healthy and clear skin.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Stressed that applying sunscreen is crucial for protecting skin from sun damage and reducing the risk of skin cancer.
